chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id from Ibn Abi 'Umayr from Hammad from Al-Halabi from Abu 'Abdillah (peace be upon him) said:

When a man says to his wife, 'I did not find you a virgin,' and he has no proof, it is said: He is flogged with the hadd punishment and he is allowed to remain with his wife, so that it does not contradict the first report, because the appropriate interpretation is that he is flogged with ta'zir (discretionary punishment), not a complete hadd, so that he does not harm a Muslim woman by exposure (to divorce).
ai.seo_question: What is the ruling if a husband claims his wife was not a virgin but has no proof?
ai.summary: In this hadith from al-Istibsar, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies that the husband receives a ta'zir (discretionary) flogging rather than a complete hadd, ensuring he is not fully divorced from his wife to prevent undue harm. This ruling highlights the Shia jurisprudential principle of balancing legal penalties with the preservation of marital stability, distinguishing between the strict requirements of hadd and the flexibility of ta'zir in cases of insufficient evidence.
